sentences.text: R. Shiva Kumar vs A.Ramaraj on 2 May, 2025

Author: Abhay S. Oka
Bench: Abhay S. Oka
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No._________/2025
 [Arising Out Of Special Leave Petition (Crl.) No.6059/2024]
 R. Shiva Kumar & Ors. Appel
 Versus
 A.Ramaraj Respon
 O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. Heard learned counsel appearing for the parties.
The appellants are being prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 59(1) and 52(1) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short, the 2006 Act).
We have perused both the provisions.
Maximum penalty of Rs.3,00,000/- is payable for both the offences.
In view of Section 69 of the 2006 Act, the offences are compoundable.
Even if the trial was to go on and appellants were to be convicted, they will be liable to pay penalty of Rs.3,00,000/- for each offence.

Now, the appellants have deposited total amount of Rs.6,00,000/-
with the Trial Court.
Therefore, we direct that the offence subject matter of CC No.1219 of 2020 on the file of learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Egmore, Chennai stands compounded.
3. The appeal is accordingly allowed.
4. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

..........................J. (ABHAY S.OKA) .........................J. (UJJAL BHUYAN) NEW DELHI;
MAY 02, 2025.
